st: Soak the smoked fish in hot water for 15 minutes, then flake it and remove any bones.
Put the cassava leaves and [[3 cups]] water in a large pot. Boil for 30 minutes until tender.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] palm oil in a pan and cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the onion mix, fish, whole chili and [[1 tsp]] salt to the leaves.
Stir [[0.25 cup]] peanut butter with a ladle of hot cooking liquid until smooth and pour it in.
Cover and simmer on low for 40 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Remove the whole chili, taste and adjust salt.
Serve hot with rice or chikwangue.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Return the chicken and add the palm butter, [[2 cups]] water, whole chili and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
The sauce will be thick and dark with oil on top. Chicken must reach 165°F (74°C).
Remove the whole chili. Serve with rice, fufu or chikwangue.

ing: whole tilapia or firm fish fillets
st: Rub the fish with the lemon juice, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Rest 10 minutes.
Mix the onion, tomatoes, chili, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and cut into 4 large squares.
Place fish on each leaf and cover with the vegetable mixture.
Fold into tight packets and tie with twine, or wrap in foil.
Steam over simmering water for 35 minutes, or grill over medium coals, turning once.
Check that the fish is opaque and flaky, at 145°F (63°C).
Open the packets carefully since steam escapes. Serve with chikwangue or rice.
Mix the cassava flour with [[2 cups]] warm water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a thick paste. Cover and ferment in a warm place for 12 hours, or skip for a milder loaf.
Cook the paste in a pot over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until it becomes a smooth, thick dough.
Let it cool until you can handle it.
Soften the banana leaves over heat and cut into 4 large squares.
Shape the dough into 4 rolls. Wrap each tightly in leaves and tie with twine.
Bring [[10 cups]] water to a boil in a large pot and lower in the bundles.
Boil gently for 90 minutes, turning once, until firm.
Cool, unwrap and slice. Serve with [[1 tbsp]] palm oil and flaked smoked fish.
Bring [[3 cups]] water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Whisk the cassava flour and cornmeal with [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until smooth.
Pour the paste into the boiling water slowly, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
Cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Keep turning and pressing the dough against the pot for 8 minutes until it is stiff, smooth and pulls from the sides.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 3 minutes.
Shape the fufu into balls with wet hands.
Drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] palm oil and serve hot with the spinach and a stew.
Slice the plantains on a slant into pieces about 0.5 inch thick.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Fry the plantains in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden with crisp edges.
Drain the plantains on paper towels.
Cook the onion and chili in a little of the oil in the same skillet for 2 minutes.
Pile the hot plantains on a plate and top with the onion and chili, then serve.
Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar into [[1 cup]] warm water. Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Add the yeast water and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch down the dough and pinch off golf-ball-size pieces. Roll into smooth balls.
Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the balls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve warm.
